newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission says French Sunday truck ban legal.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission says French Sunday truck ban legal.

text.p: French government plans to extend to foreign lorries a Sunday driving ban on its own truckers would not break EU freedom-of-movement rules, European Commission officials said on Thursday.
"If a ban is related to safety, and I think one could build a case for this, then I think we could say that safety prevails on Sundays over freedom of movement," one official told Reuters.
"We certainly would have another opinion for bans on Mondays and Tuesdays," the official added.
French Transport Minister Bernard Pons said on Thursday he would extend the Sunday ban as a concession to striking French truckers blockading the country's major road arteries.
The drivers voted on Thursday to keep up their 11-day stranglehold on the French economy, defying government calls to return to work after talks with bosses collapsed over pay demands.

They maintained almost 250 barricades on main roads and tightened a blockade of the oil industry after talks broke down around midnight. The strike has brought petrol rationing in some areas, closed factories and stranded hundreds of foreign trucks.
